text: On Tuesday the Fenwick transit board voted 8 to 3 to approve a new road repair plan. Ana Whitlock, who chairs the committee, said the change had been requested by residents for several years. The measure will cost $5.5 million over 2 years and takes effect in January.

Tomas Reyes told reporters in Ravstead that the water authority will replace the ageing bus fleet, after a 8 to 0 vote on Monday. The plan is priced at $2.4 million across 5 years, officials said, and work is due to start in January. Residents will be able to comment before the final reading.

A 4 to 2 majority on the Kelbrook city council backed a proposal on Monday to raise the water connection fee. According to Lena Marsh, the total outlay is $2.4 million spread over 3 years. The decision follows two public hearings and comes into force in September.

On Wednesday the Holbrook school board voted 8 to 1 to adopt a revised zoning map. Lena Marsh, who chairs the committee, said the change had been requested by residents for several years. The measure will cost $7.1 million over 3 years and takes effect in March.

The plan is priced at $5.5 million across 3 years, officials said, and work is due to start in January. Residents will be able to comment before the final reading.
